description:
FILED s538a (Opus, 2026-11-13) while fixing pack 'w' above UV_MAX (cl/pack-impl.pl _pack_ber).  PRE-EXISTING: main
381d9063 (MAIN-READY-89) and the s538a tree answer the same.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3; the s538a worktree's scratch/s538a/pr2/packw-nv.pl):

    print unpack("H*", pack("w", 2**70)), "\n";      # perl: 8180808080808080808000
    print unpack("H*", pack("w", 1e20)), "\n";       # perl: 8aebe3d7c5d698c08000

  PCL: dies "Can only compress unsigned integers in pack" at the first line.

pp_pack.c's 'w': an IOK value or one below UV_MAX_P1 takes the UV loop; a POK string takes w_string (is_an_int:
digits, spaces, a leading '+', a '.'-fraction ignored -- "1e21" is refused); an NOK value above UV_MAX takes the
NV floor-division loop and is NEVER refused for its exponent.  cl/pack-impl.pl stringifies the argument first
(`my $orig_s = "$raw"`) and refuses `$orig_s =~ /[eE]/ && $v >= 2**64`, so a NUMBER whose perl stringification uses
an exponent dies.  The pack implementation cannot ask perl's POK/NOK flags; PCL's values do carry the difference (a
Lisp number vs a string) -- the runtime could pass it, or pack-impl could test `$raw` with the one
number-vs-string predicate PCL already has.  _pack_ber (s538a) already encodes such an NV exactly (sprintf '%.0f' ->
div128) once the refusal lets it through.  LOW (huge NV operands to 'w' are rare).  Family: pack.t's 'w' rows.
subject: DIVERGENCE (pre-existing): `pack("w", N)` of a NUMBER above 2**64 whose string form has an exponent (`2**70`, `1e20`) dies "Can only compress unsigned integers in pack"; perl encodes it (its NV floor-division path) -- the check meant for a STRING like "1e21" cannot tell a number from a string in cl/pack-impl.pl
